simple.meaning: עֹמֶר (ʻômer) appears 14 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with priesthood. The occurrence trail connects the name with divine acceptance.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Ruth, Job, beginning at Exodus 16:16. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, priesthood, land, wilderness, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֹמֶר (H6016) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עֹמֶר through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עֹמֶר (ʻômer) / H6016 is tracked through Exodus 16:16, Exodus 16:18, Exodus 16:22, Exodus 16:32. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

He shall wave the sheaf before Yahweh, to be accepted for you. On the next day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
On the day when you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a male lamb without defect a year old for a burnt offering to Yahweh.
“ ‘You shall count from the next day after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven Sabbaths shall be completed.

When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”
When she had risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don’t reproach her.
So that they go around naked without clothing.

definitions.short: properly, a heap , i.e. a sheaf ; also an omer , as a dry measure
definitions.full: H6016. omer I. עֹ֫מֶר noun masculine Lev 23:11 sheaf ( swath , row of fallen grain, Wetzst Z. f. Ethnol. 1873, 273 (Syriac Dreschtafel) , against him Vogelst Landwirthschaft in Pal, 61 who translates heap of sheaves ); — ׳ע absolute Deut 24:19 ; Lev 23:11-12 , 15 , construct 23:10 ; figurative of food (absolute) Job 24:10 ; plural עֳמָרִים literal Ruth 2:7 , 15 . II. עֹ֫מֶר noun masculine Exod 16:22 omer (compare Arabic small drinking cup or bowl ; relation to I. ׳ע obscure); — a measure, only Exodus 16; — the measure itself 16:18 ; 16:32 ; 16:33 ; amount measured 16:16 ; 16:22 ; = 1/10 ephah 16:36 ; ᵐ5 γόμορ .
